previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a 58-year-old male with a history of acute myeloid leukemia in remission, post-transplant chronic graft-versus-host disease, BOOP, cardiomyopathy, and chronic kidney disease, was admitted for a recurrent left-sided perianal abscess with persistent pain, dehydration, and symptomatic hypotension. He underwent incision and drainage with placement of a Malecot drain, which was later downsized. He was treated with intravenous fluids, vancomycin, and piperacillin-tazobactam, later narrowed to oral amoxicillin-clavulanate. His acute kidney injury from dehydration improved with rehydration, and his metabolic acidosis resolved. His home heart failure medications were held initially due to hypotension and restarted sequentially. He was discharged home with the drain in place, on a plan for antibiotic continuation, drain care, and follow-up. Oxygen therapy was adjusted to 1 liter continuously and 3 liters with exertion due to borderline hypoxemia.

==============
ACTIVE ISSUES:
==============
# Mechanical fall: Patient reports becoming entangled in his 
oxygen tubing and fell on his right shoulder and then had a 
syncopal event with LOC. Initially presented to OSH and CT 
head/neck there were negative. CT chest and abd/pelvis non 
contrast with some mild stranding around rectum and colon, but 
no discrete abscess. Syncopal fall most likely due to 
dehydration and hypotension (see below). 

# Right humeral fracture: Xray showed 3 part fracture of the 
surgical neck of humerus without dislocation. He was evaluated 
by orthopedic surgery who did not recommend surgery. He should 
continue non-weight bearing and use the cuff and collar sling at 
all times. He will follow-up with orthopedics. Pain required 
uptitration of tylenol to 1g TID and oxycodone 5mg Q3H. 

# Hypotension: Initially presented to ED with hypotention into 
SBP of ___ and reported temperature of 101 at home; received IV 
ciprofloxacin in the ED but further antibiotics were held upon 
admission. Most likely due to dehydration in setting of diarrhea 
and antihypertensives. Patient hydrated with IVF and home 
furosemide, metoprolol, isosorbide, and hydralazine were held. 
Full infectious studies were obtained but no sources were found. 
Patient improved without antibiotics and SBP at discharge in the 
140s. Patient will need home CHF regimen restarted sequentially.

# Acute kidney injury: Creatinine elevated to 4.6 from baseline 
of 3.5-4.0 on admission most likely pre-renal in setting of 
dehydration from diarrhea. Creatinine 3.9 at discharge after IVF 
and holding home lasix and CHF regimen. 

# Non-anion gap metabolic acidosis: HCO3 on day of discharge 13 
with Cl of 110, most likely due to NS IVF administration.

# Chronic diarrhea: Patient has long history of chronic diarrhea 
s/p extensive work-up with no clear cause. He did report 
increasing diarrhea prior to admission but diarrhea improved 
during hospitalization.

TECHNIQUE:  Single axillary view of the right shoulder.

COMPARISON:  Same-day right shoulder radiographs ___ at 01:00.

FINDINGS: 

Single provided axillary view of the right shoulder demonstrates a comminuted
fracture through the proximal right humerus, with the major fracture line
appearing to traverse the humeral surgical neck.  There is anterior
displacement of the distal humerus by approximately 1 shaft's width.  There is
of large free fragment measuring 2.5 x 0.8 cm adjacent to the inferior aspect
of the humeral head.  The humeral head is not dislocated and appears in normal
anatomic relationship with the glenoid.

IMPRESSION: 

At least a 3 part fracture of the surgical neck of humerus.  No dislocation.

EXAMINATION:  RENAL U.S. PORT

INDICATION:  Evaluate for hydronephrosis in a patient with acute on chronic
kidney injury.

TECHNIQUE:  Grey scale and color Doppler ultrasound images of the kidneys were
obtained.

COMPARISON:  CT torso from ___.

FINDINGS: 

The right kidney measures 10.2 cm. The left kidney measures 10.5 cm. There is
no hydronephrosis, stones, or masses bilaterally.  Normal cortical
echogenicity and corticomedullary differentiation are seen bilaterally.

The bladder is moderately well distended and normal in appearance.

IMPRESSION: 

Exam limited due to patient body habitus, but no hydronephrosis is present.
